description: This case study is the EPA page describing water sector emergency response tabletop exercises run with state drinking water and wastewater programs, and its lessons learned fact sheet for exercises held in 2009, 2010 and 2011 (document 817-R-12-005, May 2012). The stated goal of the exercises is to raise awareness of the importance of water and wastewater services and the need for coordinated planning within a state. The page invites states that want to run a Water Emergency State Exercise to contact the EPA outreach address. The fact sheet is a 368 KB PDF, but the file itself was blocked when fetched, so the specific lessons are not described here. Coverage: three state exercises across three years, with national relevance. Access: free web page and PDF; licence not stated. Caveats: a tabletop exercise is discussion-based, not an operational event, and this record rests on the landing page only. It informs scenario design for utility emergency response and interdependency drills, and should be read together with the utility-focused incident action guidance of the EPA, which is related but not yet catalogued.
